To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

“Fish species and development specific requirements for fish protection and downstream migration must be considered in the planning of hydraulic engineering structures, as well as the associated bypasses and downstream passages.

“the design and layout of fish protection and bypass facilities have to take into account the behavior, the size, the swimming performance and the proportions of different fish species and developmental stages”.

The fish protection and downstream fish passage measures are to be designed in such a way that the fish can be guided through the facility in a way that is appropriate to their species, their age and their behavior.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the question of how the design and layout of fish protection facilities can be optimized for individual species and developmental groups, in order to ensure effective fish protection and downstream migration in the long term.
the question of whether and how fish protection and downstream fish passage facilities can be designed to ensure effective protection of the different species and their developmental stages.
the following questions: How can the behavior of different species be influenced to ensure their protection and downstream passage?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the design and the hydraulic conditions of fish protection and passage facilities are to be adapted to the species and developmental stage of fish to be protected, as well as the ecological situation of the site.
there is no such thing as a universally applicable fish protection and downstream facility.
the fish protection and downstream facilities should be designed to meet the needs of all species and age groups that are expected to pass through the hydropower plant (Chap. 2.4).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
fish passage facilities must be species and development stage specific.
the fish passage design should be as specific as possible for the species to be protected.
the fish protection and downstream facilities should be designed to meet the specific requirements of each species and each stage in the development of the fish.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for a given fish species, a certain level of protection can be achieved by means of an appropriate design.
the fish species-specific requirements must be taken into account in the design and construction of fish protection facilities.
fish behavior and fish performance are not the only factors to consider in the design of fishways.
